name: FreeSurfer mri_glmfit group analysis
purpose: Performs general linear model (GLM) analysis in the volume or the surface, including estimation and inference, and can run simulation for correction for multiple comparisons.

inputs.statement: The input data file has each frame as a separate input.
inputs.quote: Path to input file with each frame being a separate input.

inputs.statement: Global design matrix specified with a FreeSurfer Group Descriptor File (FSGDF).
inputs.quote: Specify the global design matrix with a FreeSurfer Group Descriptor File (FSGDF).

inputs.statement: One or more contrast matrix files in ASCII text.
inputs.quote: Specify one or more contrasts to test. The contrast.mat file is an ASCII text file with the contrast matrix in it

inputs.statement: Surface-based smoothing requires --surf; otherwise the input is treated as a volume.
inputs.quote: If the data are surface-based, then you must specify --surf, otherwise mri_glmfit assumes that the input is a volume

conditions.statement: Data must be assembled by resampling each subject's data into a common space and concatenating subjects into a single file.
conditions.quote:
Resampling each subject's data into a common space.

Concatenating all the subjects' into a single file.

conditions.statement: The same FSGD used with mris_preproc must be used, maintaining subject order.
conditions.quote: Same FSGD used as with mris_preproc. Maintains subject order!

conditions.statement: DODS is specified in the tutorial example and is the default.
conditions.quote: DODS is specified (it is the default).

conditions.statement: If data have not been cached, the same operations can be performed manually.
conditions.quote: In the case that you have not cached the data, you can perform the same operations manually using the two commands below.

steps.statement: Create an FSGD file for the design; it is a simple text file not generated by FreeSurfer.
steps.quote: The FSGD file is a simple text file you create. It is not generated by FreeSurfer.

steps.statement: The tutorial contrast has one value for each parameter (four values in its example).
steps.quote: There is one value for each parameter (so 4 values).

steps.statement: Assemble previously cached data using mris_preproc with the FSGD, target fsaverage, hemisphere, and output file.
steps.quote:
mris_preproc --fsgd gender_age.fsgd \
--cache-in thickness.fwhm10.fsaverage \
--target fsaverage \
--hemi lh \
--out lh.gender_age.thickness.10.mgh

mri_glmfit \
--y lh.gender_age.thickness.10.mgh \
--fsgd gender_age.fsgd dods\
--C lh-Avg-thickness-age-Cor.mtx \
--surf fsaverage lh \
--cortex \
--glmdir lh.gender_age.glmdir

steps.statement: Optionally run mri_glmfit-sim on the GLM directory for clusterwise correction.
steps.quote: All these steps are performed with the command mri_glmfit-sim:

checks.statement: The completed GLM has its output subdirectory under the glm directory.
checks.quote: When this command is finished the glm directory will contain a sub-directory called lh.gender_age.glmdir.

checks.statement: There is a subdirectory for each specified contrast, named after the contrast matrix file without the .mtx extension.
checks.quote: There will be a subdirectory for each contrast that you specify. The name of the directory will be that of the contrast matrix file (without the .mtx extension).

checks.statement: mri_info can be run on the assembled data to find its dimensions.
checks.quote: Run mri_info on lh.gender_age.thickness.10.mgh to find its dimensions:

exceptions.statement: Temporary directories or log files starting with tmp may appear and can be ignored.
exceptions.quote: You may also see some temporary directories (with names starting with tmp) or log files, which you can ignore.

exceptions.statement: You cannot specify both --X and --osgm, and a contrast cannot be specified with --osgm.
exceptions.quote: You cannot specify both --X and --osgm. A contrast cannot be specified either.

exceptions.statement: Do not use --prune with --sim; instead run the non-sim analysis with --prune and pass the created mask to the simulation.
exceptions.quote: Do not use with --sim. Rather, run the non-sim analysis with --prune, then pass the created mask when running simulation.

outputs.statement: Outputs are saved to the glmdir directory, with beta.mgh containing all regression coefficients.
Per-contrast outputs include gamma.mgh, F.mgh, and sig.mgh.
outputs.quote:
gamma.mgh - contrast (G above)
F.mgh - F-ratio
sig.mgh - significance from F-test (actually -log10(p))

outputs.statement: The final binary mask is saved as mask.mgh when a mask is used.
outputs.quote: The final binary mask will automatically be saved in glmdir/mask.mgh

outputs.statement: A log of execution parameters is saved as mri_glmfit.log.
outputs.quote: mri_glmfit.log - execution parameters (send with bug reports)

parameters.statement: Spatial smoothing can be performed between resampling subjects into common space and concatenating their data.
parameters.quote:
Resampling each subject's data into a common space.

Concatenating all the subjects' into a single file.

Spatial smoothing (can be done between 1 and 2).

parameters.statement: --fwhm smooths input with a Gaussian kernel at the given FWHM in mm.
parameters.quote: Smooth input with a Gaussian kernel with the given full-width/half-maximum (fwhm) specified in mm.

parameters.statement: --cortex specifies that the analysis only be done in cortex, zeroing out the medial wall.
parameters.quote: "--cortex" specifies that the analysis only be done in cortex (ie, medial wall is zeroed out).

parameters.statement: --sim-sign accepts abs, pos, or neg, with abs as default.
parameters.quote: sign is either abs (default), pos, or neg.
